question: The presence of vital reaction (including vascular response, haemorrhage into tissues, and early inflammatory cell infiltration) in a wound confirms that the injury was inflicted during life (ante-mortem), whereas post-mortem wounds show none of these features.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This statement is TRUE. Vital reaction — vascular response, haemorrhage into tissues, clot formation, and early inflammatory infiltration — is the hallmark of ante-mortem injury. Post-mortem injuries show passive blood extravasation without clot, no oedema, and no inflammatory response. Distinguishing ante-mortem from post-mortem injuries is one of the most important forensic pathology tasks.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. Vital reaction is the collective term for the biological responses of living tissue to injury: active haemorrhage with clot formation, vascular dilatation, oedema, and early neutrophil infiltration (microscopically). Post-mortem wounds show passive ooze without clot, no vascular response, and no inflammatory cells. These findings are central to determining the timing of injury.
